name: slide-title
text: Cruise operations span three moments

name: slide-context
text: Harborline links passenger plans with work managed onboard.
BEFORE SAILING
Plan the trip
Find a sailing, reserve a cabin and assign dining seats to each ticketed guest.
ON BOARD
Run the ship
Handle crew shifts, guest service, boarding, maintenance and muster activity.
WHEN PLANS CHANGE
Coordinate response
Review port impacts, notify affected passengers and dispatch follow-up work.
One sailing record connects guest, crew and operations workflows.

Frame the scope around the trip lifecycle rather than a feature list.

Sources: README.md; docs/ASE-AGILE-REPORT.md; docs/BACKLOG-AND-SPRINTS.md.

name: slide-title
text: Adaptive Software Engineering approach

name: slide-context
text: Short build-and-review cycles incorporated changing project requirements.
Speculation
Set a working vision and record uncertainty about inventory, safety, payments and external data.
Collaboration
Translate passenger, crew, captain and manager needs into role-specific workflows.
Learning
Implement against the server and review behavior, tests and operational edge cases.
Adaptation
Add guest-level dining, scoped permissions, captain-issued faults and port recovery.
Illustrative development approach documented in the project materials; no formal user study is recorded.

Describe the project process as an iterative development record, not a completed user study.

Sources: docs/ASE-AGILE-REPORT.md; docs/BACKLOG-AND-SPRINTS.md; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

name: slide-title
text: Role boundaries shape the work

name: slide-context
text: Access is checked in the application and again by the server.
Passenger
Manage a booking, guest dining seats, itinerary notices and service cases.
Crew
View permitted shifts, accept eligible jobs and record progress or resolution.
Captain
Create faults, review port recovery and lead operational response.
Manager
Configure sailings, inventory and sailing-scoped staff permissions.
Staff permissions can be limited by action and by sailing; consequential changes are attributed in activity history.

Emphasize separation of responsibilities and sailing-scoped authorization.

Sources: README.md; server.js; app.js; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: Booking and dining are checked per guest

name: slide-title
text: Booking and dining are checked per guest

name: slide-context
text: Cabin reservations and dining seat assignments persist on the server.
CABIN BOOKING
Reserve an available cabin
Availability is checked on the server. Collision protection prevents two requests from claiming the same cabin.
Idempotency keys make repeated reservation requests safe to process.
DINING SEATS

One ticketed guest
= one seat
Guests may choose seats in different meal batches. The server checks guest count, seat availability, blocked seats and batch capacity.
AVAILABLE
FILLED
BLOCKED
The guest count is the seat count: no extra or missing dining assignments.

Call out the booking collision safeguards and the exact ticket-to-seat rule, including split meal batches.

Sources: README.md; server.js; app.js; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

name: slide-title
text: Ship readiness extends beyond reservations

name: slide-context
text: Boarding, safety and maintenance actions are attached to operational records.
BOARDING
Manifest & check-in
One-time ticket check-in against the sailing manifest. Camera scan depends on browser support; manual and keyboard-scanner entry are available.
SAFETY
Muster & drills
Authorized staff can open a drill or event and record guest accountability at configured muster stations.
MAINTENANCE
Equipment & due work
Keep an equipment register, recurring service plans, completion notes and next due dates.
Actions are attributed to staff and recorded in local activity history.

Summarize ship-operation modules while making clear that station configuration and safety response require operator validation.

Sources: README.md; server.js; app.js; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: A connected local MVP, with a clear next phase

name: slide-title
text: A connected local MVP, with a clear next phase
Harborline connects passenger booking to shipboard work through role-checked APIs, persistent records and action history.
Validate
Test priorities and task flows with representative passengers, crew, captains and managers.
Connect
Integrate authoritative sailing, identity, manifest, payment and notification services.
Harden
Set backups and audit retention; review accessibility, security and vessel safety procedures.
Prototype boundary: seeded sailings, local infrastructure, no default payment; operational safety needs vessel-operator validation.

Close with the implemented value and the work required before a cruise operator could rely on the system.
